stories.title: Power struggle stalls BJP district president appointments in UP:Disputes between top leaders over candidates delay naming district chiefs in 5 areas
stories.summary: The politics of Purvanchal is considered incomplete without caste and pressure politics. This time BJP appears to be caught in this political maze. The party's stalwarts have linked their prestige to the appointment of 5 district presidents in Purvanchal. In Chandauli, there is an open tussle between Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and former state president Mahendranath Pandey. In Deoria, the egos of 2 former state presidents (Surya Pratap Shahi and Ramapati Ram Tripathi) clashed. While in Gorakhpur-Varanasi, CM Yogi and PM Modi's likes and dislikes have completely stalled the matter. This is also affecting the party's functioning. What is the reason for this tug of war? With less than a year left for assembly elections, when will the 5 district presidents be announced? Read in our special report... First District - Chandauli District President appointment stuck between Brahmin vs Thakur Chandauli is the home district of former Union Minister Dr. Mahendranath Pandey and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Party sources say Pandey wants to remove the current district president, Kashi Singh. He wishes to appoint a Brahmin face as president. Their camp believes that Kashi Singh did not work properly in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Even after being the Kshatriya district president, the Thakurs voted for SP. This led to the defeat of two-time MP Dr. Mahendranath Pandey. Kashi Singh belongs to the Defence Minister's camp. Now the announcement of the district president is stuck in the tug of war between Rajnath Singh and Dr. Mahendranath's camps. The special thing is that the party had made Pandey the in-charge of state organisational elections. Under his supervision, 93 district presidents have been declared in the organisational elections. However, the appointment of the district president is stuck in his home district itself. Second District - Deoria Ramapati says, ‘Whoever I advocate for will become president’ In Deoria, Pintu Jaiswal, a close associate of former state president Ramapati Ram Tripathi and Sadar block chief, was almost certain to become the district president. Tripathi had also approved Jaiswal's name to state president Pankaj Chaudhary. However, Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi, MP Shashank Mani Tripathi and 2 local MLAs opposed Pintu's appointment. However, in the case Ramapati Ram Tripathi says, ‘I did not ask anyone to make Pintu Jaiswal the district president’. Ask whoever is saying this and why they are saying so. As far as advocacy is concerned, if I advocated for someone, they would definitely become president. The argument against Pintu was that he joined the BJP in 2021 before the panchayat elections. The party made him block chief. Now, if I were made district president, it would send the wrong message to workers. This matter went from Lucknow to Delhi, and Pintu could not become the district president. Now the party is looking for a name that everyone agrees on. Third District - Ambedkarnagar State President looking for a Kurmi-Brahmin face BJP wanted to promote district vice president Rana Randhir Singh to make him president here. However, state president Pankaj Chaudhary's argument was that Faizabad division is a Kurmi and Brahmin-dominated area. SP has Kurmi and Brahmin leaders here. The party has only appointed a Kurmi district president in Barabanki of Faizabad division. Not a single Brahmin has been made district president. In such a situation, Chaudhary suggested making a Kurmi or Brahmin face the district president instead of Rana, which would help in securing the vote bank. This is the reason why the announcement of the district president's name could not be made in Ambedkar Nagar as well. Fourth District - Varanasi District President will be appointed based on PM's preference Hansraj Vishwakarma is the district president in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency, Varanasi. The party has also made him a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC). Active in politics for 34 years, Hansraj is an important face of the backward classes in the area. Therefore, a search is on for a strong alternative to replace him. According to sources, the decision of the district president in Varanasi will only be made after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's green signal. It is by the Prime Minister's wish that Hansraj has remained district president for three terms. Fifth District - Gorakhpur Metropolitan President passed away last June In March 2025, Devesh Srivastava was declared Metropolitan President in Gorakhpur. However, he passed away from a heart attack in June 2025. Now the position of Metropolitan President is vacant here. There is no political manoeuvring happening here. The Metropolitan President will be appointed only with CM Yogi's preference. Therefore, everyone is waiting for his signal. 93 names approved so far BJP has divided UP into 98 organisational districts. The party released the first list of 70 district presidents on March 16, 2025. Devesh Srivastava, the district president of Gorakhpur, included in this list, passed away in June 2025. Meanwhile, Gonda district president Amar Kishore Kashyap was removed after a video of him with a female worker went viral in the party office. This left 68 district presidents. After this, 14 more names came forward on November 26 and 11 district presidents on February 26 this year. In this, Iqbal Bahadur Tiwari was made president in Gonda. However, the appointment of district presidents in Chandauli, Deoria, Varanasi, Ambedkar Nagar and Gorakhpur has not been made yet.

stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'women will get ₹40,000 if party forms govt':SP chief hits out at ‘Dhurandhar’, claiming BJP funding films
stories.summary: “These people have decided on a cabinet expansion during Navratri. It is just an attempt to pacify those who are upset. Now that the budget has been fully spent, they are making ministers. Funds are being released quickly to several departments. One department has even approved tenders worth ₹1,000 crore, but it is unclear what has actually been delivered,” said SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday, taking a swipe at the Yogi government’s likely cabinet expansion. Akhilesh was speaking at the Murti Devi–Malti Devi Women Honour Ceremony in Lucknow, where several women were felicitated. His wife and Mainpuri MP Dimple Yadav were also present. He reiterated that if voted to power, his party would give ₹40,000 annually to women and revive the Samajwadi pension scheme. Amid the controversy over the film ‘Dhurandhar’, he alleged that the BJP is now funding films to defame opposition parties. The film ‘Dhurandhar: The Revenge’, released on March 19, features a character named Atif Ahmed, resembling real-life mafia Atiq Ahmed. Leaders from Congress and SP have termed the film propaganda. Dimple Yadav said that in the “new India”, women feel unsafe and fearful. Referring to the Ankita Bhandari case in Uttarakhand, she said such incidents leave deep wounds and raise concerns about the country’s progress. Key points from Akhilesh’s speech: 1. ‘Not a green corridor, but a wasted corridor’ in Lucknow Akhilesh said the Defence Minister wants to do good work for Lucknow, but CM Yogi has built a “wasted corridor” instead of a green corridor. He claimed it lacks space for pedestrians and does not meet proper standards, despite costing ₹7,000 crore. 2. ‘Election setting has already begun in UP’ He alleged that preparations and “settings” for elections have already started in UP, including the posting of officials. He also claimed irregularities in previous elections. 3. ‘LPG cylinder depends on luck now’ Mocking the situation, he said getting an LPG cylinder depends on luck, otherwise people must stand in queues. He also accused BJP leaders of irregularities in cylinder distribution. 4. ‘Law and order have collapsed in UP’ Akhilesh blamed the administration and police for deteriorating law and order, citing incidents in Gorakhpur, Varanasi and Mathura. He alleged political misuse of the police and rising corruption. 5. ‘PDA strength troubling BJP’ He claimed that the strength of PDA (backward, Dalit, minority alliance) is worrying the BJP, and alleged plans of large-scale deployments and election manipulation. 6. ‘If Shankaracharya not spared, anyone can be insulted’ He criticised police actions, saying if even religious leaders like Shankaracharya are not spared, anyone can be insulted. He also questioned the process of appointing the DGP.

stories.title: Shringar Gauri temple opens after a year:2 km queues as women raise ‘Free Gyanvapi’ slogans, Australian devotee joins chants
stories.summary: A large number of devotees gathered on Sunday for darshan at the Maa Shringar Gauri temple inside Varanasi’s Gyanvapi complex, with queues stretching nearly 2 km. The temple opens for devotees only once a year on the fourth day of Chaitra Navratri, and will now reopen next year. The four women plaintiffs in the Gyanvapi case also arrived to offer prayers, raising slogans of “Free Gyanvapi”. They have moved court seeking recognition of the site as a temple. Tight security arrangements were in place due to the heavy footfall, with devotees allowed entry under strict supervision. During the 25-minute worship, vermillion and sandalwood paste were applied to the ancient, damaged stones of the shrine, while mantras were chanted. The premises echoed with chants of “Har Har Mahadev”, accompanied by damru beats. Among the devotees was Maria from Australia, who joined in chanting praises of the Goddess. See 3 photos... Regular worship banned after 1992 Regular darshan and worship of Maa Shringar Gauri continued until 1992. Following the Babri demolition in Ayodhya, access was restricted due to security concerns. Since then, the temple has been opened for darshan only once a year, on the fourth day of Chaitra Navratri. On August 18, 2021, five women filed a petition in a Varanasi court seeking permission for regular worship at the site. Acting on court orders, a survey was later conducted within the premises. After the survey, the Hindu side claimed that a Shivling was found in the basement, while the Muslim side maintained that it was a fountain. The petition is led by Delhi-based Rakhi Singh. The other petitioners—Sita Sahu, Manju Vyas, Laxmi Devi and Rekha Pathak—are residents of Varanasi.

stories.title: CM Yogi distributes nursing appointment letters to 1,100 women:Dy CM Pathak targets opponents, says era of job loot is over
stories.summary: Yogi Adityanath distributes joining letters to 1,097 female and 131 male nursing officers in Lucknow on Sunday, saying at a program held at Lok Bhawan that receiving appointment letters during Navratri reflects the growing strength of women. He said, The days are gone when it was believed that nothing would come of opening medical colleges or nursing colleges. Earlier, a parallel government of mafias used to run in medical colleges. Every department had a mafia. The department ran as he wished. Now, instead of mafias, 'One District, One Medical College' has been established. Meanwhile, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak said, Nurses are made for service. So you should not get angry, you have to serve the patients. You people never worry. If there is any problem, tell us. You are like our family's daughters and brothers. Some have been posted far away. If you don't find a place to live, tell us too. Pathak also said- Earlier, people from the same community used to get jobs. Connections (jugaad) worked in every job, but now jobs are obtained through intellect and skill. Mafia who looted jobs are now fleeing to save their lives. Those who watched dances in Saifai. They are also troubled. In commerce, it is said - bad money drives good money out of circulation, so we have to go among the public and explain the difference. Now, 5 major points from Yogi's address 1. ‘Earlier hospitals ran on God’s mercy’ He said Indian nursing staff are in high demand globally (Japan, Germany, Korea, Europe). From 1947–2017, UP had only 17 medical colleges; now there are 81 (government + private). Earlier, the nursing and paramedical sectors were neglected, and hospital facilities depended largely on fate. 2. Story of Gorakhpur nursing school He recalled a nursing school in Gorakhpur that had only one faculty member. When the principal feared closure affecting 100 trainees, he arranged an honorarium to continue operations. He said 35 ANM/JNM institutes closed during the SP government are being revived, and construction of 31 nursing colleges has restarted. Nursing is the backbone of healthcare. 3. Major rise in medical seats He said healthcare improved under the double-engine government: maternal mortality now matches the national average; 3.5 crore people linked to Universal Health Coverage; 14 crore ABHA IDs created. Nursing seats increased by 7,000, paramedical by 2,000, MBBS seats from 5,390 to 12,700, and PG seats from 1,221 to 5,056. PPP-mode medical colleges are also running. 4. UP to supply nurses nationwide During Navratri, distributing appointment letters to many women reflects empowerment. With a population of 25 crore, UP aims to provide nursing manpower for the entire country. He suggested offering nursing education in multiple Indian languages like Tamil, Marathi, and Kannada. 5. ‘No discrimination in jobs or schemes’ He said reservation rules for SC, ST, and OBC are fully followed. In the last 9 years, 9 lakh government jobs have been provided without recommendation or transactions. Recruitment is done transparently through commissions under monitoring. Deputy CM highlights role of nurses Deployment in 14 districts including Kanpur The nursing officers who have received joining letters will be deployed in medical colleges of Agra, Kanpur, Prayagraj, Meerut, Jhansi, Gorakhpur, Ambedkarnagar, Kannauj, Azamgarh, Jalaun, Saharanpur, Banda and Badaun, along with JK Cancer Institute and Cardiology Institute, Kanpur.

stories.title: Fake IAS has married not once but 25 times:Victim's father alleges serial marriage fraud; vows to get justice for his daughter
stories.summary: He has married not once, but 25 times. He extorted money by posing as a fake IAS officer and also ruined my daughter's life. He left us with nothing. Every day a new story about him comes to light. This is what the father-in-law of the fake IAS officer, who lives in Gorakhpur, has to say. Half of his body is paralysed, and he remains confined to bed. Only a few years after suffering paralysis, another calamity struck, leaving the entire family shattered. On condition of anonymity, he told Dainik Bhaskar that he will not rest until the man who ruined his daughter’s life is punished. He also explained how the family fell into the fake IAS officer’s trap, how the relationship was arranged, and how the truth eventually came to light. The father-in-law of the fake IAS said, I have 3 daughters and one son. I have married off 2 daughters. Meanwhile, I became paralyzed. Half of my body doesn't work, so I started looking for a match for my youngest daughter. My youngest daughter has graduated. IAS profile shared in community group He said his elder daughter, who lives in Delhi, told him about a community group where someone shared the profile of an IAS officer named Pritam Kumar Nishad from Ludhiyat Mohalla in Etawah. The profile stated he was 32 years old and posted as an SDM in Manikpur, and that his family did not want dowry, only a beautiful bride. Hearing this, he felt the match was suitable and asked his daughter to proceed with the talks. Family visits Etawah to verify groom After his elder daughter spoke to Pritam Kumar Nishad about marriage, she arranged a phone conversation with him as well. He later visited Gorakhpur in December 2025, where the family met him, and he liked the girl upon seeing her. As talks progressed, family members went to Etawah to verify details. They found a 2BHK house in Ludhiyat Mohalla, where Pritam said he lived with his sister and that the house was in her name. He told them his financial condition had been poor earlier, but he was planning to sell the house and buy a new one. Dowry demand made before wedding When Pritam Kumar Nishad was asked about his village, he said it was 35 km away across a river and claimed it was very backward, adding he was the first boy from there to become an IAS officer. This helped him gain the family’s trust, and they were satisfied with the match. The wedding was fixed for March 11, 2026. Although he initially refused dowry, after the date was finalised, he demanded money, citing wedding and reception expenses, saying important guests would attend. At his insistence, ₹15 lakh was given to him one month before the wedding. 'Government of India' written on car Relatives expose groom’s fake identity Pritam showed videos in his defense The girl's father said that in his defense, Pritam provided a video. That video contained Pritam's interview. A YouTuber had interviewed him after he became an SDM, which had been running on his channel for four years. After this, Pritam said that his relatives are jealous and they don't want him to get married. After being convinced, the farewell ceremony was completed on March 12, 2026. Villagers called and revealed the truth The girl's father said that shortly after, several more calls came from Pritam's village. They also provided proof of Pritam's fraud. They said that Pritam had run away from the village. He has defrauded many people. He has married 25 times by lying. Reached groom’s house after farewell The girl’s father said they were frightened after the farewell and asked their daughter to keep sharing her location. Three hours later, his son, nephew, and elder daughter left Gorakhpur by car. Pritam Kumar Nishad reached his house in Ludhiyat Mohalla, Etawah, around 9 PM, while the girl’s family arrived at 11 PM. They found people at his house intoxicated, and Pritam himself returned with red eyes. Truth revealed after interrogation SSP Dr. Kaustubh said, A case has been registered. After investigating the family's allegations, action will be taken against the accused.

stories.title: New claims in Farsa Baba death case:Disciples allege truck ran him over intentionally; questions raised over police hiding the container
stories.summary: Whether the death of Farsa Wale Baba aka Chandrashekhar Singh (45) in Mathura is an accident or murder... this mystery is getting more complicated. Baba's supporters are calling it murder, while police are saying it was an accident. According to the theory stated by police the Baba was checking a container with Nagaland number plate when a truck bearing Rajasthan number plate hit the container from behind. Baba died after being caught in the collision. Baba received information that cattle was being transported by truck Supporters stated that Baba had received information regarding cattle being transported by truck. He chased the truck on a bike with his two companions. They overtook and stood in front of it. They started checking the container. That's when a truck coming from behind deliberately crushed Baba. Baba's companions were also targeted but they narrowly escaped. However, the DIG stated, There were no cattle in the trucks. The Nagaland number truck contained soap-shampoo and the Rajasthan number truck had oil. The Rajasthan number truck was damaged in the accident. The driver died during treatment, while regarding the container and its location This has not been traced yet". In this situation, Baba's supporters have raised questions that if the container really had soap-shampoo, why did the police keep it in an unknown location? They said that CCTV footage from the highway will reveal the truth. Read what the disciples who accompanied Baba said. Hariom said – the collision was deliberate, the container had cows Hariom, a disciple who lives at Baba’s cowshed, said, “Around 3 am on Saturday someone called Farsa Wale Baba and informed him that cattle were being transported from the National Highway near Kosi. After receiving the information, Baba took me and Kanha on his motorcycle and reached the spot”. He added, “As soon as Baba arrived, a container with a Nagaland registration number started speeding towards Delhi. Baba chased it and stopped it near the Navipur area”. He further stated, “Baba got down from the bike and was checking the container when a truck with a Rajasthan number coming from behind rammed into him at high speed. It wanted to crush all of us, but Baba pushed us away and came under the truck himself”. He also said, “If there was nothing illegal in the container, why did the people inside try to flee?” He claimed that the container was carrying cows. That is why the truck moving behind deliberately hit Baba. Another companion said - There was adequate light at the accident spot Kanha, another companion who was with Baba, said, “You can go and see how much light there is at the place where the incident occurred. The truck running in the middle directly hit Maharaj Ji after seeing him. Maharaj Ji didn't get a chance. After the collision, the container people ran away. They were Muslims, that's why the police let them go. Otherwise, the public would have killed them”. He added, “Maharaj Ji used to go on patrol every day. This is just a conspiracy. At this same point, three years ago, Sonu Sarpanch, who was involved in cow protection, was also killed. Kanha claims that if the administration checks CCTV footage, it will show that there were cows in that vehicle. Why hasn't the police shown the recovery of the container yet”. Now find out what the police and administration are saying Who is Farsa Wale Baba? Chandrashekhar Baba's home is in Ajnaukh village in the Chhata area on Barsana Road in Mathura. He has been serving cows for many years. Local people say, “Farsa Wale Baba was always dedicated to cows. Initially, whenever there was any problem regarding cows in the Barsana area, people would tell Baba. He gradually became famous in the area by helping cows”. Farsa Wale Baba, who dedicated his life to cow service, was so feared among smugglers that as soon as they learned of his presence, they would abandon the illegally transported cattle and run away. Baba's elder brother Keshav Singh said, “Younger brother was 45 years old. Originally from Sirsaganj Langra of Firozabad. He had become a Baba at the age of 10. In the family, we were the only two brothers. I have 4 sons, 4 daughters-in-law, 7 grandsons and 6 granddaughters. Baba never married”. He further stated, “We live in Ayodhya. Earlier, Baba also used to live with us in Ayodhya. Later he came to Mathura”. He has also demanded death penalty for the culprits. Understand the complete matter... Farsa Wale Baba died after being crushed by a truck in Kosikalan's Kotvan police station area on Saturday. A video has emerged after the accident. In this, Baba is lying on the ground. A sword with its sheath is lying near him. The front part of the Rajasthan number truck appears damaged. Its driver Khurshid, a resident of Alwar, also died during treatment in Agra. News of the incident spread like wildfire in the area. Thousands of people came out on the highway in Mathura's Chhata town. Angry people placed Baba's body and blocked the Delhi-Kolkata highway. They started demanding encounter of the accused. The police who arrived to take possession of the body and clear the traffic jam were chased away by people. They also pelted stones, in which some policemen were injured. People vandalized 5 to 6 police vehicles. Windows were broken. Seeing the situation getting out of control, police resorted to lathi charge. Tear gas shells were fired. CM Yogi took cognizance of the matter Meanwhile, people took Baba's body to the gaushala located in Ajnaukh village. They put forward 6 demands including building a memorial for Baba before the administration. The DM assured that a memorial site will be built at the place of Baba's cremation. After this, Baba's last rites were performed. CM Yogi also took cognizance of the matter. While directing officials to take strict action, he said, “The accused will not be spared”. Meanwhile, late Saturday night, 16 rioters including Hindu Raksha Dal worker Daksh Chaudhary have been arrested for causing disturbance regarding Farsa Baba's death.

stories.summary: The accused in the murder of a student at UP College in Varanasi was produced in court under tight security on Saturday evening. Police feared that lawyers and students might assault the accused. Therefore, the police tried to make him run, but he stumbled because his leg was fractured. Following this, police personnel carried him into the courtroom. The Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) sent Manjeet to jail for 14 days. Police had arrested Manjeet on Friday for the murder of student Surya Pratap Singh. However, his associate Anuj Singh, who allegedly helped him, is still absconding. See Manjeet's court appearance in 2 pictures... Manjeet said - Student used to do ragging Police interrogated the accused named Manjeet Chauhan before presenting him in court. During this, he revealed that Surya Pratap Singh along with his friends used to rag him. Manjeet said, “Surya Pratap Singh and his associates often troubled me and my friends in the name of ragging. They would physically assault us. On the day of the incident, March 20, we also had an argument on the college campus. There were threats and intimidation”. He added, “In anger and revenge, along with my companion Anuj Singh, I fired 4-5 rounds at Surya Pratap near the administrative building. This resulted in his death”. Sharp argument between protesting students and ADM Meanwhile, on Saturday (March 21), ADM Alok Verma reached to persuade the students who were protesting against Surya Pratap's murder at UP College. During the talks, there was a sharp argument between ADM and the students. After this, the students put forward 5 demands. The officials assured to take the charter of demands from the students and send it to the government. These 5 demands were put forward by students to ADM Now know the complete matter... Student had returned to college on Friday after 20 days The deceased father Rishi Dev Singh is a driver at Atulanand School. His mother Kiran Singh is an assistant at Atulanand School. Surya has two sisters, one is married while the other sister is still studying. Surya Pratap had chickenpox 20 days ago. Due to this, he was not coming to college. After recovering, he came to college on March 20 only. That's when he was murdered. Crime Scene and Subsequent Events… It was 11 o'clock in the morning. Students were studying in their respective classes. Suddenly, BSc student Surya Pratap Singh was shot and killed on the college campus. BA second-year student Manjeet Singh Chauhan shot him in filmy style in front of the principal and students. A student recorded a video of the live incident. After the murder, the accused fled after throwing the pistol in a garbage heap. After this, everyone had just one question in their mind that why did Manjeet kill Surya? It was reported that Surya used to call senior students to the hostel. He would rag junior students. Manjeet had complained about this to the principal. The principal had summoned both of them. On Friday, after meeting with the principal, there was a dispute between Manjeet and Surya. In which Manjeet rolled up his shirt sleeves, then Surya grabbed Manjeet's collar while hurling abuses. At that time, friends intervened and stopped them. Manjeet went to his home. From there, he came to college with a pistol along with a friend. He parked his Pulsar bike near the gate outside the college. Then, as soon as he saw Surya in the arts faculty corridor, he opened fire on him. He fell down, yet he continued shooting at him with the pistol. Manjeet's leg broke after jumping from 12 feet height After the murder, Manjeet felt that he would be caught if he escaped through the gate, so he jumped from the roof to avoid this. His leg broke when he jumped from a height of about 12 feet. His bike was parked at the gate, but seeing himself surrounded, he ran towards Airport Road even with his broken leg. He took a lift in an e-rickshaw to reach Gilt Bazar intersection and then turned off his phone. After this, he tried to get treatment after reaching a deserted place. After breaking his leg, he could not flee outside the city. Meanwhile, police pressured the family members for his arrest. Angry students created ruckus in college premises After the incident, angry students created a ruckus on the college campus. They broke chairs inside the campus. After about 4 hours, the police got the college gate opened. Students and teachers were evacuated from the college by forming a cordon. Three professors were injured in stone pelting by students. Police chased away the protesting students with lathi charge. Meanwhile, parents fainted upon seeing the body of their only son. Now know about Surya Pratap Singh... 21-year-old Surya Pratap Singh was from Ghazipur district. He completed his education till 8th standard from Ghazipur. He came to UP College to study from 9th standard. Since then, he had been studying here. He was very talented in studies. He passed his 12th examination in PCM from UP College itself with first division. Then he cleared the entrance exam and got admission in BSc Mathematics here. Fellow students said that he was very friendly. He kept himself busy with studies. After BSc, he wanted to do research in MSc Mathematics from here. His dream was to go into academics. Case registered against accused Manjeet Chauhan The accused student Manjeet Chauhan is a BA second year student. Manjeet is from Chandmari area of Varanasi itself. He already had a case under section 323 registered at Shivpur police station, while his associate Anuj also has several cases registered against him. The accused, who gets into fights over small matters, is of an aggressive nature. He has a bad boy image on social media. He calls himself a mafia on Instagram. He is also well-known in local police stations like Bhojubir, Shivpur and Bada Lalpur. He runs an 1818 gang on social media. He had written in his Instagram bio “Your respect remains only as long as it doesn't hurt my self-respect. Jai Maa Bhawani”.

stories.title: Film ‘Dhurandhar’ sparks row over Atiq Ahmed portrayal:Chargesheet in Umesh Pal Murder mentions Pakistan link
stories.summary: A brief 7–8-minute appearance by a character named Atif Ahmed in the film Dhurandhar: The Revenge has sparked a political and factual debate. The reel character closely resembles the real-life mafia don Atiq Ahmed from Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The film recreates his murder in a manner strikingly similar to the killing of Atiq and his brother Ashraf in April 2023, while attributing the sequence of events to a conspiracy involving National Security Advisor Ajay Sanyal. In contrast, in Uttar Pradesh, it is widely believed that the decline of mafia dominance, including that of Atiq, resulted from CM Yogi Adityanath’s stringent crackdown. The film also portrays Atif Ahmed as having links with Pakistan’s intelligence agency ISI, depicting him as a major arms supplier, counterfeit currency operator, and political influencer. These claims have led leaders from the Congress and Samajwadi Party to label the film as propaganda. Former SP MP Dr. S.T. Hasan stated that no Indian investigative agency has confirmed such allegations, calling it an attempt to generate controversy for publicity. Amidst these claims, here is a breakdown of what the film shows versus documented realities. Fact 1: Alleged ISI links and arms supply Film portrayal: The film depicts Atif Ahmed procuring AK-47 rifles through Pakistan’s ISI, facilitated by Baloch mafia networks. Reality: Atiq Ahmed was murdered on 15 April 2023. Fifteen days earlier, Prayagraj Police filed a chargesheet in the Umesh Pal murder case, naming Atiq and his brother Ashraf in arms trafficking. According to the document, Atiq claimed he had ample access to weapons and acknowledged links with ISI and Lashkar-e-Taiba operatives. The chargesheet states that weapons were airdropped via drones in Punjab and then routed through local agents to Atiq’s network. The same consignments allegedly reached militants in Jammu and Kashmir. Atiq also indicated possible recovery points for weapons. Based on these statements, police registered an FIR mentioning ISI-supplied arms, including AK-47 rifles, a .45 bore pistol, a sten gun, and even RDX. A .45 pistol was reportedly used in the Umesh Pal murder, while 58 Pakistan-made 9mm cartridges were recovered. Fact 2: Criminal network operated from jail Film portrayal: Atif Ahmed is shown managing his operations from inside prison, coordinating with ISI officials and directing smuggling activities, including drugs via Nepal. Reality: This aspect aligns closely with documented incidents. Following the 2007 Raju Pal murder, Atiq spent most of his time in various prisons, including Naini (Prayagraj), Deoria, Banda, and Chitrakoot. In April 2013, while lodged in Deoria Jail, Atiq’s associates abducted Lucknow-based businessman Mohit Jaiswal and brought him into the prison. There, Jaiswal was brutally assaulted, suffering fractures in his fingers, and coerced into transferring ownership of his companies, MJ Infra, to associates Farooq and Zaki. The case gained national attention, leading to Atiq’s transfer to Bareilly Jail in December 2018 and subsequently to Sabarmati Jail in Gujarat in 2019. Fact 3: Counterfeit currency via Nepal route Film portrayal: The narrative links Atif Ahmed to a massive counterfeit currency operation orchestrated by Dawood Ibrahim, prompting the Indian government’s demonetisation move in November 2016. Reality: No formal case was registered against Atiq Ahmed for circulating fake Pakistani currency through Nepal into Uttar Pradesh. However, multiple cases involving hawala transactions were filed. Investigations revealed that Atiq was involved in extortion, routing funds through shell companies, transferring them abroad, and reintroducing them into India via alternative channels. Fact 4: Political influence in UP Film portrayal: The film suggests that Atif Ahmed played a role in influencing government formation in Uttar Pradesh. Reality: Atiq Ahmed did wield significant political influence. He was first elected MLA from Allahabad West in 1989 and retained the seat in 1991, 1993, 1996, and 2002. In 2004, he became an MP from Phulpur on a Samajwadi Party ticket. Even after imprisonment in the Raju Pal murder case, he remained politically active. However, there is no evidence supporting two key cinematic claims: that his political rise was funded by counterfeit currency operations, or that he directly influenced the formation of state governments. Why is the film being called propaganda ? Former IPS officer Lalji Shukla, who investigated multiple cases involving Atiq during his tenure in Prayagraj, offered a nuanced perspective. He acknowledged that counterfeit currency does enter India from Pakistan, often through Bangladesh and Nepal routes, and noted that such consignments were intercepted during his posting in Bahraich. However, he clarified that Atiq’s name never directly surfaced in these cases. On weapons, Shukla stated that Atiq had a known fascination with firearms and that multiple weapons were seized from him over time, including a .30 pistol licensed in another individual’s name. He added that while the film draws inspiration from reality, it cannot be treated as factual. Individuals involved in violent crime may also engage in smuggling or financial crimes, but such links must be proven. Senior journalist and writer Manoj Rajan Tripathi also emphasised the film’s disclaimer stating that any resemblance to real individuals is coincidental. He pointed out that despite over 175 cases registered against Atiq, none conclusively established arms smuggling from Pakistan during his lifetime. Tripathi further noted that the film focuses on selective elements while omitting major incidents, including the Raju Pal and Umesh Pal murder cases and other serious allegations. As such, he argues, Dhurandhar: The Revenge should be viewed as a dramatised narrative rather than a factual account.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:EC announces Assembly poll schedule; WB elections in 2 phases; Row over ‘Pandit’ question in Sub-inspector exam in UP more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. EC announces Assembly poll schedule; WB elections in 2 phases The Election Commission on Sunday announced the schedule for Assembly elections. Polling in Kerala, Assam and Puducherry will be held in a single phase on April 9. Tamil Nadu will also vote in a single phase on April 23. West Bengal will go to the polls in two phases — on April 23 and April 29. Votes will be counted on May 4. 2. Row over ‘Pandit’ question in Sub-inspector exam in UP: Government orders probe, action promised if community dignity found hurt A question in the Uttar Pradesh Police Sub-Inspector exam linked the word ‘Pandit’ with opportunism, triggering protests from political leaders and the Brahmin community. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak promised strict action. BJP MLAs demanded investigation, calling it insensitive and possibly deliberate. The UP Police Recruitment Board is probing the issue while warning against viral fake papers. Exams are underway across 1,090 centres with strict security; two candidates died travelling to centres. 3. Prasad being cooked on stoves at Sita Temple in Ayodhya: First such crisis in 35 years; gurukuls forced to close LPG cylinder shortage has forced temples and gurukuls to switch to traditional stoves. In Ayodhya, meals for thousands continue on wood-fired stoves, while Varanasi’s Annapurna Temple kitchen shut down for the first time in 35 years. Authorities are working to restore normal operations. 4. Epstein gang plotting 9/11-style attack to blame Iran Today marks the 16th day of the US-Israel-Iran war. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has said that if Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is alive, they will hunt him down and kill him. According to Al Jazeera, the IRGC said, "If the child killer is alive, we will pursue him with all our might and kill him." 5. Ghaziabad’s Harish shifted to AIIMS Delhi for euthanasia: Emotional farewell at home, Brahma Kumari applies tilak, says forgive everyone Harish Rana, in a coma since a 2013 accident, was quietly moved from Ghaziabad to AIIMS Delhi after the Supreme Court approved passive euthanasia. Family gave an emotional farewell; a video of prayers and tilak went viral. Doctors will gradually remove life support under supervision, allowing a natural end. The family expressed gratitude to supporters and clarified no lethal injection will be used. 6. Kuldeep hugs Vanshika after varmala: Cricketer takes 7 vows with childhood friend; watch royal wedding VIDEO Kuldeep Yadav tied the knot with his childhood friend Vanshika in a royal ceremony at The Savoy Hotel, Mussoorie. He arrived with the wedding procession in a vintage car, wearing a golden sherwani. Traditional rituals were performed, and a grand reception is planned in Lucknow on March 17. 7. Top 10 companies’ market value shrinks ₹4.48 lakh crore The value of the country's 10 largest companies by market capitalisation decreased by ₹4.48 lakh crore in last week's trading. During this period, SBI's value decreased the most. SBI's market cap decreased by ₹89,306 crore to ₹9.66 lakh crore. HDFC Bank's market cap decreased by ₹61,715 crore to ₹12.57 lakh crore. 8. 7 UPSC candidates in UP make false claims of success:Took suitcase from MLA, conducted roadshows; truth exposed 24 hours later UPSC results released on March 6 saw multiple false claims of selection, with candidates from UP, Bihar, and other states claiming IAS success despite failing prelims or not appearing. Cases included Shikha Rani, Priyanka Chaudhary, Divya Tanwar, and others. Investigations revealed mistakes, doctored documents, and edited admit cards. Officials and psychologists cited ambition, social pressure, and fear of failure as reasons. Past incidents from 2014–2022 show similar fraud, prompting calls for stricter verification and public awareness. 9. ₹950 cylinder getting sold in black for ₹3,500 in UP:Bhaskar gives money to supplier, who says prices will rise further Amid the ongoing LPG shortage linked to the US–Israel–Iran conflict, black marketers in Uttar Pradesh are selling domestic cylinders at ₹3,500 and commercial ones at ₹5,000, 2–3 times the official price. Investigations in Lucknow revealed hawkers charging heavily, exploiting weak monitoring, and diverting cylinders from regular supply. Despite government helplines and committees, black marketing persists, leaving households struggling to access cylinders. Officials said action would be taken if locations were reported. 10. Jay Shah breaks silence on Pak, B'desh's T20 WC boycott saga International Cricket Council (ICC) chairman Jay Shah addressed the uncertainty that dominated headlines ahead of the T20 World Cup 2026. The tournament, which ended on 8 March, saw India lift a record-extending third title, beating New Zealand in the final.

stories.title: Boy starts barking 4 months after dog bite:Father takes him to temple fearing black magic, locals rush him to hospital
stories.summary: A 17-year-old boy in Mirzapur started barking four months after being bitten by a dog. His family believed someone had cast black magic on him. On the evening of March 14 (Saturday), they took the boy to a temple priest. Seeing the crowd there, the boy began barking loudly and shouting “ghost… ghost”. Saliva started dripping from his mouth. Seeing this, people from the surrounding area gathered there. Locals advised the family to take him to a doctor instead of performing exorcism rituals. After this, an ambulance was called by dialing 108 and the boy was sent to the hospital. A doctor at the local hospital suspected rabies and referred him to Varanasi. Doctors said the child had received two anti-rabies injections, but the family did not get the third one. Because the vaccination course was incomplete, he became a victim of rabies. The entire incident is from the Kachhwan police station area. Know the full matter- There is the Shri Ram–Janaki temple near Jamua crossroads. On Saturday evening, Guru Nanak from Jogipurwa reached there carrying his younger brother in his arms to get exorcism done. Their father Bhailal was also with them. When people asked about the situation, the father said that four months ago the boy had gone to his maternal home. There he was bitten by a dog. At that time, one injection was given at a private clinic and the second at CHC Kachhwan. However, the third injection could not be administered because it was not available at the hospital. Before moving ahead in the news, please participate in the poll On March 13 (Friday), the boy suddenly started experiencing severe pain in his head. After that he became frightened and began behaving strangely. He started barking and became afraid on seeing water. He kept getting scared again and again and kept saying “ghost… ghost”. We thought someone had done black magic on him. That is why we brought him to the temple for exorcism. Seeing the crowd at the temple worsened his condition. Seeing the child’s condition, local resident Badri Singh called 108 and summoned an ambulance. He was immediately sent to the Community Health Centre in Kachhwan. After initial treatment there, doctors referred him to Varanasi. Youngest among 6 siblings Father Bhailal said his wife has died. He himself suffered paralysis four years ago. Since then, the elder son Nanak has been supporting the family by repairing mobile phones and doing tile work. This boy is the youngest among three brothers and three sisters. He used to work at a tea stall in the village. The middle son is mentally ill, while all three daughters are married. Now learn about rabies... Rabies is a dangerous viral infection that affects the brain and central nervous system. It is caused by the Lyssavirus and usually spreads through the bite or scratch of an infected dog, cat, monkey or other animals. In rare cases, infection can also occur through organ transplantation. If vaccination is not done on time, the virus spreads in the body and attacks the brain, leading to symptoms such as behavioural changes, fear, anxiety, fear of water and seizures. According to doctors, once symptoms appear in humans, rabies is almost always fatal. Therefore, it is extremely important to get vaccinated immediately after an animal bite. If treatment is started at the right time, the infection can be prevented. Rabies does not exist in some countries, but related viruses are found in bats in several places, which can also be dangerous for humans. Therefore, experts say any animal bite should never be taken lightly and immediate medical help should always be sought.

stories.title: Major LPG black marketing racket exposed in Lucknow:88 cylinders seized in raid; gas shortage shuts 80% hotels, restaurants in UP
stories.summary: Amid an ongoing LPG shortage in Lucknow, a major case of black marketing has come to light. A joint team of the district administration and the supply department raided Abhinandan Resort on Mohan Road and uncovered an illegal gas refilling and storage racket. A large number of domestic and small cylinders were recovered from the spot. An FIR has been registered at Kakori police station under the Essential Commodities Act against several individuals, including the gas agency proprietor, the manager and the resort owner. According to District Supply Officer Vijay Pratap Singh, 88 cylinders were seized during the raid. These included 65 empty domestic cylinders of 14.2 kg capacity and nine filled domestic cylinders. The team also recovered 14 small cylinders of five kilograms each. Officials also seized a Bolero Maxi Truck (UP32 QN 5729), which was allegedly being used to transport the cylinders. Anger among customers over gas shortage The shortage of LPG cylinders has triggered widespread anger among customers. A day earlier, a young man reportedly lay down on the road in front of a gas delivery vehicle in protest. While residents have been standing in long queues for hours outside gas agencies, complaints of black marketing have also surfaced in several parts of the city. Illegal refilling racket operating from resort The raid at Abhinandan Resort was carried out on Saturday by a joint team led by District Supply Officer Vijay Pratap Singh. During the inspection, officials found evidence that LPG cylinders were being illegally refilled and stored inside the resort premises. Authorities said locals had tipped them off about the illegal activities taking place at the site. During the operation, officials recovered a large quantity of cylinders from the premises. Officials noted that while citizens are forced to stand in queues throughout the day for LPG cylinders, illegal trade in the commodity continues simultaneously. Case registered against agency operator and resort owner The supply department has initiated action against those found involved in the illegal activities. An FIR has been lodged against Manju Kannaujia, proprietor of Aseem Bharat Gas Agency and wife of Samajwadi Party leader Sonu Kannaujia, and agency manager Munna alias Iqtada Hussain. Surendra Kumar, owner of Abhinandan Resort and a resident of Manas Vihar, Alamnagar, Bolero Maxi Truck owner Jameel Ahmed and Sahil have also been booked under the Essential Commodities Act at Kakori police station. Joint team conducted the operation The raid was conducted by a joint team comprising officials from the district administration and the supply department. The team included Regional Food Officer Alambagh Suresh Kumar Saroj, Ravindra Kumar Singh, Parvez Akhtar, Supply Inspector Kaushalendra Kumar Pandey, Satyam Mishra and BPCL sales officer Digvijay Kumar Singh. Officials counted and seized all the cylinders recovered from the spot, and a detailed investigation into the racket has been initiated. Authorities said complaints regarding illegal sale and refilling of LPG cylinders are also being received from other locations. Gas crisis hits hotels and restaurants across Uttar Pradesh The LPG shortage has also severely affected the hotel and restaurant industry across Uttar Pradesh. According to RK Sethi, chairman of the UP Hotel and Restaurant Association, nearly 80% of hotels and restaurants in the state have shut down due to the disruption in the supply of commercial gas cylinders. In Kanpur alone, around 60% of the business has come to a halt, he said. An order was issued late Saturday evening to resume the supply of commercial cylinders, but industry representatives say it is still unclear when the situation will return to normal. Sethi said the hotel industry has almost come to a standstill due to the lack of commercial gas cylinders. In some places, attempts are being made to cook food using wood and coal. Uttar Pradesh has around 14,000 hotels and nearly 20,000 restaurants, many of which have been severely affected by the shortage. Guests unable to get even tea Sethi said his group runs eight hotels in Kanpur, of which seven have remained closed for the past four days. “The situation is such that we are unable to serve even tea to guests staying in our hotels,” he said. He added that the use of wood and coal for cooking could increase pollution, which is why their use is limited. According to Sethi, his eight hotels alone are suffering losses of nearly ₹5 lakh every day. Kanpur has around 200 hotels and 250 banquet halls, many of which are struggling to host previously booked events due to the gas shortage. Wedding menus altered due to gas shortage The gas crisis has also disrupted social events. Sethi said a wedding feast for 700 guests was held at a hotel on Friday where the menu included imarti and jalebi, but the sweets could not be prepared due to the gas shortage. Instead, boondi laddoos had to be served. Similarly, an iftar party had planned to serve balushahi, but it could not be prepared due to the lack of gas. Laddoos were eventually served instead. Hotel operators claim commercial LPG cylinders are reportedly being sold in the black market for as much as ₹5,000. Restaurants shut in Kanpur Kanpur has nearly 350 to 400 hotels and around 700 restaurants, many of which have also been forced to close due to the gas shortage. The city’s well-known Pandit Restaurant has suspended both lunch and dinner services and has remained closed for the past four days. Its operator, Pranav Pandey, said he runs two restaurants but had to shut them down due to the unavailability of gas cylinders. “We have completely stopped the food segment for now. We are not using wood or coal either because environmental concerns must also be considered,” he said, adding that the restaurants will remain closed until the supply situation improves.

stories.title: Ghaziabad’s Harish shifted to AIIMS Delhi for euthanasia:Emotional farewell at home, Brahma Kumari applies tilak, says forgive everyone
stories.summary: 'Go now, forgiving everyone and asking forgiveness from all...alright...' Harish Rana from Ghaziabad, who was allowed passive euthanasia by the Supreme Court on March 11, has now been shifted to All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi. Before leaving his home in Rajnagar Extension, family members gave him an emotional farewell. “Forgive everyone and ask forgiveness from everyone before you go,” said Brahma Kumari Lovely while gently placing her hand on Harish’s head. She also applied a sandalwood tilak on his forehead before he was taken on his final journey. A video of the farewell from the family’s Ghaziabad home has gone viral on social media. During the emotional moment, several family members were seen with tears in their eyes. Emotional farewell at home Harish’s father Ashok Rana also apologised to family members and said the decision had to be taken despite their reluctance. Harish has been in a coma for the past 13 years. On Saturday, he was quietly shifted to AIIMS Delhi for the procedure. The family kept the entire transfer process confidential, and even neighbours in the society were unaware. According to a close acquaintance, the family took Harish to Delhi in a private vehicle. Following the Supreme Court’s decision, AIIMS will now make arrangements for a dignified end to Harish’s life. Doctors will gradually remove him from the life-support system. What's in the video? A 22-second video circulating on social media shows Harish lying on a bed while a woman applies a sandalwood tilak on his forehead. She gently strokes his head and tells him to forgive everyone and seek forgiveness before leaving. Mother, sister and brother became emotional and started crying When Harish was taken from the Ghaziabad flat to AIIMS, his mother, younger brother and sister became emotional. His parents, Nirmala and Ashok Rana, said they were deeply grateful to everyone who supported them during the long legal and medical struggle. We apologize to everyone, God gave us this to witness. We just want that wherever our son is, in whichever afterlife he remains, we will never be able to forget him. Father said - Our close ones, relatives, doctors, lawyers who advocated for us in court and everyone supported us a lot. We will remain grateful for everyone's support. Rana family connected with Brahma Kumaris The Rana family is associated with the Brahma Kumaris spiritual organisation. After sharing their pain with Brahma Kumari Lovely, she helped them connect with a lawyer. The family said the High Court had earlier rejected their plea, but the Supreme Court granted permission, which they believe ended their son’s prolonged suffering. “We cannot watch his pain anymore. He cannot even tell us where it hurts,” the father said. The family clarified that Harish will not be given any lethal injection. Instead, doctors at AIIMS will gradually remove the feeding tube under medical supervision, allowing a natural end. They said they will continue to give him water like someone observing a fast and will bring his body back home respectfully for the final rites. Mother's tears won't dry, says - my son never shared his pain Harish’s mother said it was heartbreaking to see her son in such a condition. “No parent would want their child to go through this. I used to massage him every morning and evening and tell him stories from home,” she said. She added that sometimes they would wait for hours for a small response—like a blink, a sneeze, or slight movement near his eyes—to feel reassured that he was still alive. Find out how Harish reached this condition... Harish Rana was born in Delhi and was studying BTech at Panjab University in Chandigarh. In 2013, during his final semester, he fell from the fourth floor of his hostel building. The accident left him paralysed and in a coma. Since then, he has been unable to speak or respond to his surroundings. Doctors diagnosed him with Quadriplegia, a severe condition in which a patient survives only with the help of a feeding tube and ventilator. According to doctors, the chances of recovery in such cases are extremely low. Due to being bedridden for 13 years, he has also developed severe bedsores and his condition has deteriorated over time. The Supreme Court directed that passive euthanasia be provided in his case, marking a significant decision in India’s legal and medical history.

stories.title: Prasad being cooked on stoves at Sita Temple in Ayodhya:First such crisis in 35 years; gurukuls forced to close
stories.summary: The ongoing shortage of LPG gas cylinders is now affecting temple kitchens as well. Food arrangements in several temples and community kitchens in Ayodhya and Varanasi have begun to suffer. In many places, food for saints, students and devotees is now being prepared on traditional wood-fired stoves, while some kitchens have been temporarily closed after running out of gas. In Varanasi, the kitchen of the Annapurna Temple has fallen silent for the first time in 35 years. Meanwhile, some gurukuls in Ayodhya have had to suspend operations because of the shortage. Dainik Bhaskar visited several temples in both cities to assess the situation. Temple kitchens in Ayodhya turn to traditional stoves The gas shortage in Ayodhya has begun to affect the preparation of offerings and meals served to thousands of saints and students. At temples such as Hanumangarhi Temple, Shri Ramvallabhakunj Ashram, Lakshman Kila and Siyaram Kila, temple food is now being cooked on traditional stoves. Similarly, Sita Rasoi, located in the Amawa Temple complex, is entirely dependent on traditional cooking methods. In the large courtyard of the Amawa Temple, which is located near the Ram Mandir, rows of traditional stoves have been installed. Through these, meals and breakfast are prepared daily for approximately 8,000 to 10,000 devotees visiting the temple to see Ramlala. Pankaj, the manager of the Amawa Temple associated with Sita Rasoi, said the kitchen has become completely dependent on traditional stoves. ‘Devotees are still receiving sufficient prasad. Until the gas problem is resolved, we will continue to rely on these stoves,’ he said. Temple food quality remains unaffected Despite the shortage, temple authorities say the quality of offerings and prasad has not been compromised. According to Ramesh Das, senior priest of Hanumangarhi Temple, the temple has been cooking offerings and prasad on a traditional stove for the past two days, but the daily rituals continue as usual. He added that the offerings of curd, rabri and imarti to Lord Hanuman remain unchanged. Food for Ramlala is still being cooked using LPG cylinders, and regular offerings are continuing without disruption. Another priest, Santosh Kumar Tiwari, said that all temple activities are proceeding normally despite the fuel shortage. Gurukul forced to close due to cylinder shortage The shortage has severely affected educational institutions as well. The Prabhu Shri Ram Kripa Gurukul Veda Pathshala has been temporarily closed due to the lack of gas cylinders. New admissions were about to begin, but arranging food for the 20 students currently studying there has become difficult. The institution’s principal, Acharya Abhishek Tripathi, said cylinders are not available and calls to suppliers are going unanswered. Students depend on stoves and community kitchens At Shri Vashishth Gurukul in Darshan Nagar, food for 110 Vedic students is now being prepared on traditional stoves. In its main branch at Vasudevghat in Ayodhya Dham, arrangements have been made to cook meals for 60 students using whatever gas supply is available. When shortages become severe, students travel to Shri Ramvallabhakunj Ashram for meals, or depend on community kitchens run in nearby temples. Dr Dilip Singh, director of Shri Vashishth Gurukul, said they have informed the authorities about the shortage. ‘We have been receiving calls from the department, but the supply of gas cylinders has still not resumed,’ he said. Meanwhile, Rajkumar Das, head priest of Shri Ramvallabhakunj Ashram, confirmed that due to the shortage, temples have intensified the use of traditional kitchens where stoves are used to prepare offerings and daily prasad. Dr Virendra Kumar Mishra, president of Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Charitable Hospital, said that Ayodhya has not faced such a severe cylinder shortage since the COVID-19 pandemic period. Annapurna temple kitchen falls silent in Varanasi The impact of the LPG shortage is also visible in Varanasi. On Saturday, the stove in the kitchen of the Annapurna Temple did not light up, forcing the temple’s Annakshetra (community dining hall) to suspend food service. Devotees who arrived for meals after offering prayers were unable to receive prasad or food, and many had to return empty-handed. Cooking operations were also halted at the second branch of the Kashi Annapurna Annakshetra, located in the Bansphatak area of Varanasi, after the gas supply ran out. This is believed to be the first temple in Kashi where a community kitchen serving devotees had to shut down due to the LPG shortage. First such crisis in 35 years According to Mahant Shankar Puri, the Annapurna kitchen has been operating continuously for around 35 years, and such a crisis has never occurred before. He said the situation has arisen because LPG cylinders required for cooking are currently unavailable. The temple management said efforts are being made to resolve the problem quickly and restore food services for devotees as soon as possible.

stories.title: 7 UPSC candidates in UP make false claims of success:Took suitcase from MLA, conducted roadshows; truth exposed 24 hours later
stories.summary: The UPSC results which came on March 6th has generated a stir of controversy in the state. According to the information, 7 such candidates were claimed to be selected who had not actually succeeded in the exam. It also came into notice that MLAs and senior officials visited their homes to congratulate them. During interviews, these candidates claimed to have studied all night. However, the truth came out within 24 hours citing a complete different story. The shocking fact is that 6 candidates had not even passed the preliminary exam. Among those making claims, one girl is a GST inspector, another is working at RBI. This is the first time so many people have falsely claimed of becoming IAS. The question is why did these people make such claims? Did they think claiming could get them a job? Does UPSC take any action against those making false claims? In today's Sunday Big Story we will learn answers to such questions... First read about the false claim of the UP candidate... Shikha said - I became an IAS, in reality only cleared prelims Shikha from Bulandshahr claimed that she secured 113th rank in UPSC. Her grandfather is a peon in an inter college. He became emotional and started crying in front of the camera. This clip went viral. The heading became - 'Peon's granddaughter cracked UPSC'. Shikha kept sharing success stories in interviews. How the truth came out - Shikha from Delhi emailed UPSC that another Shikha from Bulandshahr is claiming IAS selection. Please clarify this. After this, UPSC asked Bulandshahr DM Shruti to investigate. The DM sought a report from SDM Sadar Dinesh Chandra. The investigation revealed that Bulandshahr's Shikha's full name is Shikha Rani. She had not passed the Mains exam. Shikha who was selected at 113th rank is from Delhi. She is working as BDPO in Sampla, Rohtak. After this, Shikha Rani apologized. and said, “I only saw the name, not the roll number. Meanwhile, her Father Premchand said, ”Daughter got emotional after the result, so she immediately told the family after seeing the name, that was her mistake". GST Inspector's lie - I became an IAS officer Priyanka Chaudhary from Ghazipur district called her father Neera Ram after the result was announced. She said, “Papa, I cleared UPSC. Got 79th rank. I might get IAS”. After this phone call, her father became emotional. The entire Gaurakhash village of Jakhaniya was filled with enthusiasm. Priyanka is currently posted as GST Inspector in Prayagraj. She got this job only 3 months ago. She joined on December 15, 2025. How the truth came out - Within 24 hours, it was discovered that Priyanka Chaudhary had lied. The real Priyanka Chaudhary is from Bikaner, Rajasthan. Her husband Mukesh Repswal is a 2015 batch IAS officer. He is currently posted as Deputy Commissioner in Chamba district of Himachal. Priyanka was preparing while staying with him. She achieved this success in her fourth attempt. Meanwhile after the truth came out the GST Inspector said, “No such claim was made by me. My father got emotional, which caused the misunderstanding”. The reality to this story is that she even couldn't crack UPSC's preliminary examination. Divya's success story was published in newspapers Another false claim occured at 182nd rank in UPSC. Divya Tanwar from Baghpat district claimed selection. Celebrations began in the family. Principal Ranvir Singh of Vanasthali Public School, where Divya studied, said, “Divya was hardworking since childhood. We will honor her”. Her father Ravinder Kumar is in CISF and lives in Delhi. The next day, her success story was also published in newspapers. How the truth came out - Within 24 hours, it was revealed that Divya Gehlawat from Rohtak district of Haryana was selected at 182nd rank. She lives in Sector-3 of Rohtak. Currently, she is pursuing PhD from Delhi University. After this, Divya Tanwar from Baghpat went underground. Neither did she nor any member of her family spoke about this matter. It did come to light that she had not even passed the preliminary examination. False claims made in other states in the name of candidates who became IAS in UP UP's Yashvardhan selected, MP's Yashvardhan made the claim Yashvardhan Singh's name appeared at 212th rank in the list. Yashvardhan, who lives in Nagaud area of Satna, claimed that he was successful. People gathered to congratulate his father Narendra Singh Parihar and mother Sangeeta. Media interviews started. He claimed, “I am only somewhat satisfied with this success. I will come back with a better rank in UPSC”. How the truth came out - Satna's Yashvardhan's lie was caught at the time of the result itself. Because the candidate with the same name who was selected belonged to OBC category. Whereas Satna's candidate belongs to General category. In reality, he had not even qualified the prelims. Yashvardhan Singh from the Rath area of Hamirpur district, UP was selected. He is the son of Dr. Surendra Singh, Principal of Swami Brahmanand College. Previously, he had secured 728th and 571st ranks. He completed his MBBS from KGMU Lucknow. He has reached the civil services interview stage 4 times. As soon as results came, Akanksha Singh said - I became an IAS Akanksha Singh from Bihar's Bhojpur district claimed her selection. Sweets were distributed at her home. People started coming to congratulate. Even Deputy CM Samrat Chaudhary congratulated her. Akanksha is the granddaughter of Ranvir Sena founder Brahmeshwar Mukhiya. How the truth came out - Ghazipur's Akanksha posted her documents on social media. Said that 301st rank is mine. My roll number is 0856794. Bihar's Akanksha also claimed that this roll number belongs to her. However, upon scanning the admit card, her roll number was showing as 085659. PIB clarified that Ghazipur's Akanksha is the real one. It was revealed that Bihar's Akanksha had not even passed the preliminary exam. Now let's understand the fake claims made in other states... Didn't even take the exam, claimed to become an IAS Ranjit Kumar Yadav from Shekhpura district of Bihar claimed, “I secured 440th rank. I have become an IAS. Former RJD MLA Vijay Samrat arrived with supporters. Garlanded me and gave a briefcase”. Mahuli's Station In-charge Ram Pravesh Bharti also honored him by offering sweets. Several videos of Ranjit emerged, in which he is making big claims. Elderly people standing nearby were listening to him emotionally. How the truth came out - After 2 days, it was revealed that Ranjith Kumar from Karnataka was selected at 440th rank. He is from Chikballapur district. On the other hand, Bihar's Ranjit was called to the police station over phone. He switched off his phone and fled to Delhi. Those who had posted congratulatory messages removed them. It was discovered about him that he had previously claimed 2-3 times about getting jobs. This time he hadn't even appeared for the preliminary exam. He does small jobs while living in Delhi. Documents edited, truck driver's daughter claims to become IAS Fairooz Fatima claimed to secure 708th rank in civil services examination. Since it was during Ramzan, celebrations were held at night instead of day. She was accepting greetings from people while standing in a car with sunroof. How truth came out - The truth came out within just 24 hours. It was discovered that the real Fairooz Fatima is from Kerala. The coaching institute where she studied issued a poster. After 36 hours, UPSC also confirmed the selection of Fairooz Fatima from Kerala at 708th rank. Upon further investigation, it was found that Fairooz from uttrakhand had not even passed the preliminary examination. She edited the roll number on the admit card. She also edited and created the photo that is taken standing outside the UPSC office. Farooz is currently Deputy Manager at RBI. Now the investigation of her documents in the RBI job has begun. Did these candidates do this by mistake? We asked this question to several IAS officers, read what they say... Moradabad's CDO IAS Divyanshu Patel said "Such cases come up every year in civil services. I think candidates do this for 3 reasons. Former IAS Rakesh Verma said, "This is absolutely not true. How can someone who hasn't passed the preliminary exam claim their selection by looking at the result? If two candidates with the same name pass the prelims-mains exam and reach the interview stage, they might be confused for a brief moment when seeing their name in the result. But both facts will be different. First- Their roll numbers will be different. Second- Their categories will also be different. This is how identification happens. In an institution like UPSC, two people with the same name have never been selected under the same roll number". He further said, “Police wait for someone to complain about such frauds. The person in whose name these claims are being made has nothing to do with it. Police can take action on their own, but they also avoid it”. What psychologists say... stories.title: Row over ‘Pandit’ question in Sub-inspector exam in UP:Government orders probe, action promised if community dignity found hurt
stories.summary: A controversy has erupted over a question asked in the Uttar Pradesh Police Sub-Inspector recruitment examination. The question asked candidates: ‘What would you call someone who changes according to the opportunity?’ Four options were provided, Pandit, Opportunist, Frank, and Virtuous. The question appeared in the General Hindi section of the paper. The issue triggered protests from political leaders and members of the Brahmin community, who objected to linking the word Pandit with a negative trait. Now, the question from the question paper that is causing a stir Deputy CM assures action Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said that any question that hurts the dignity of a community is unacceptable. He stated that the matter will be investigated and strict action will be taken against those responsible. BJP leaders raise objections Three BJP Brahmin MLAs, Shalabh Mani Tripathi, Prakash Dwivedi and Ramesh Chandra Mishra, along with BJP state minister Abhijat Mishra, have protested against the question. They wrote to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath demanding action. According to sources, the issue has also reached the BJP’s central leadership. At the party’s state office, several office-bearers reportedly described the incident as wrong in the presence of state president Pankaj Chaudhary. They said repeated mistakes by officials are damaging the party’s image among the public. Statement by suspended PCS officer Suspended PCS officer Alankar Agnihotri claimed the question had been asked ‘out of frustration’. He alleged that a “non-Sanatani system” is dominant in the government and said anger has grown against it. He further claimed the Brahmin community would soon fight this system. MLAs write to Chief Minister In his letter, Deoria Sadar MLA Shalabh Mani Tripathi raised four demands. He wrote that the issue does not appear to be a simple mistake but rather a well-planned conspiracy. According to him, a perception is developing among people that controversial issues are being deliberately raised targeting a particular community, which harms social harmony. Badlapur MLA Ramesh Chandra Mishra said linking the word Pandit with a negative meaning such as opportunism is inappropriate, insensitive and possibly deliberate. Banda Sadar MLA Prakash Dwivedi wrote that the word Pandit traditionally means a learned and knowledgeable person and carries religious respect. Associating it with a negative term like opportunist is wrong. Recruitment board orders investigation The Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board has taken cognisance of the issue. In a statement on X, the board said the question paper is prepared by highly confidential institutions to maintain secrecy. Officials at the board level do not see the papers beforehand, and sealed packets are opened only at the examination centres. The board said the matter is under investigation and action will be taken if anyone is found responsible. Fake paper goes viral, FIRs registered Meanwhile, a fake question paper related to the examination went viral on social media. The board clarified that the viral paper had no connection with the actual examination and warned people not to spread rumours. A total of seven FIRs were registered at Husainganj Police Station in Lucknow on March 13 and 14. The Sub-Inspector recruitment examination is being held on March 14 and 15 in two shifts, 10 am to 12 pm and 3 pm to 5 pm, at 1,090 centres across 75 districts. The recruitment aims to fill 4,543 posts. Strict security at exam centres Candidates were subjected to three-layer security checks before entering examination centres. Only admit cards and identity cards were allowed inside. In Varanasi, male candidates were asked to remove their shoes, socks and belts, while sacred threads (kalava) were cut before entry. Female candidates were required to remove jewellery, including bangles, toe rings and earrings. In a separate incident in Ambedkar Nagar, two youths died in a road accident while travelling for the examination.

stories.title: ₹950 cylinder getting sold in black for ₹3,500 in UP:Bhaskar gives money to supplier, who says prices will rise further
stories.summary: 'Look brother, gas cylinders will be available, but you won’t be able to take them. They are extremely expensive. Not two or four, we can arrange only one cylinder. A commercial cylinder will cost ₹5,000 and a domestic one ₹3,500.' These were the words of a gas hawker in Lucknow. Amid the ongoing LPG crisis in the country, triggered by the US–Israel conflict with Iran, hoarders in Uttar Pradesh have turned the situation into an opportunity. Instead of making normal deliveries, they are selling cylinders in the black market at two-and-a-half to three-and-a-half times the official price. Domestic cylinders, priced at around ₹950, are being sold for ₹3,500, while commercial cylinders costing ₹2,007 are being sold for ₹5,000. To expose this racket, the Dainik Bhaskar team carried out a ground investigation in Lucknow. Spot: Gomtinagar For the sting operation on gas cylinder black marketing, we first reached Gomtinagar. Near a park in Vivek Khand, dozens of people were standing in line for cylinders. Here we met Ramkripal, a clerk at a gas agency. People standing around him were pleading for cylinders. Taking the opportunity, we tried to strike a deal with Ramkripal. He said that currently no cylinder would be available for ₹3,000. Reporter: Has the vehicle not arrived? Ramkripal: It has reached the warehouse but hasn’t arrived here yet. If it leaves the warehouse, some work may happen. Reporter: What is the situation with commercial cylinders? Ramkripal: The situation is very bad. Reporter: What happened? Ramkripal: The rate is ₹2,200, but they are not even available for ₹3,000. Reporter: Where? Ramkripal: At Husadiya Chowk. Reporter: Bharat Gas? Ramkripal: No brother, any of them, Bharat, Indane or Indian. Reporter: I need a commercial gas cylinder. Ramkripal: Brother, I won’t lie. ₹7 lakh is due to me from Nilkanth’s place, ₹20 lakh from Indira’s and ₹20–22 lakh from Raj’s. Everyone has refused to supply gas to these people. Reporter: That is a lot of outstanding money. Ramkripal: Yes, there has been a lot of dishonesty. Earlier things were fine. Reporter: Why was so much credit given? Ramkripal: Earlier they used to take 500–700 cylinders from us. Later they started buying from others. When the outstanding amount increased, they began purchasing from third parties. Reporter: Is it available in the black market? Ramkripal: Brother, it is available for ₹2,000 in black. Reporter: Can you arrange a commercial cylinder? Ramkripal: The official rate is ₹2,200. People are ready to buy for up to ₹3,500, but even then it is difficult to get one. Reporter: Can you arrange something? Ramkripal: Yesterday I bought commercial cylinders for ₹2,500 and sold them for ₹3,500. Reporter: How? Ramkripal: I bought them here for ₹2,500 and delivered them there for ₹3,000. How many commercial cylinders do you need? Reporter: At least 50 cylinders in 15 days. Ramkripal: If his phone is on, we can talk. Reporter: Yes, please arrange it. Ramkripal: Okay, I will call. Ramkripal further said that in Gomtinagar many households receive piped gas, so some people sell their cylinders for ₹1,100–₹1,200. He assured that he would arrange cylinders by the next day. Spot: Patrakarpuram Chauraha We then moved towards Patrakarpuram intersection. On the way we met a hawker named Kallu. We asked him to arrange five cylinders. Initially he refused, but later said he could arrange one. When asked about the price, he said it would cost around ₹2,500. Kallu shared his phone number and said he could arrange the cylinder within two to three hours. Spot: Indiranagar After this we reached Surendranagar in Indiranagar. Here we met restaurant owner Manish Kumar, who had been identified as someone involved in black marketing cylinders. Reporter: Do you have any arrangement for gas? Manish: You will get it, but you won’t be able to take it. Reporter: What do you mean? Manish: It is very expensive. Reporter: No problem, call him. We need two or four cylinders. Manish: Not two or four. I can arrange only one. Reporter: Fine, get one then. Manish: It will be domestic, right? Reporter: Commercial or domestic, anything will do. Manish: Commercial will cost ₹5,000 and domestic ₹3,500. Manish initially avoided calling his contact but asked the reporter to call him later in the evening. Later he phoned back and said a cylinder would be available at 9 pm. If needed immediately, one cylinder could be collected at once. Spot: Cantt After speaking to Manish, we reached the Cantonment area. Here we struck a deal with a hawker. We paid ₹3,500 and received a commercial cylinder. When asked about a domestic cylinder, he said it could be arranged for ₹2,200–₹2,300. Reporter: How much do I have to pay? Hawker: ₹3,500. Reporter: That is very expensive. Hawker: Brother, it is not available anywhere. The hawker promised to deliver a domestic cylinder the next day at the same location. What our investigation revealed? Three major findings emerged from the investigation- District Supply Officer responds When contacted about the black marketing of cylinders, District Supply Officer Virendra Singh said, 'Send the location wherever this is happening, and we will take action.'
